quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Is driving too slowly against the law?

options.text: Yes, it is against the law.
No, it is safe for drivers who are not confident.
No, tired drivers should do this.
No, most police officers recommend it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is against the law.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is illegal in Florida. Do not drive so slowly that you block or slow down traffic that is moving at normal, safe speeds. Drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: Why should you be alert to motorcycles?

options.text: Because they are harder to see than cars.
Because they rarely use their headlights.
Because motorcycle drivers are less skilled.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because they are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge the distance to a motorcycle or how fast it is going. Always watch carefully for motorcycles.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely dangerous.
Nothing to worry about.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bikers, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to the road helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: You see a "Drawbridge" sign with a flashing yellow light. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.
Speed up quickly.
Drive carefully and continue.
Stop only if you see a boat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light at a drawbridge means the bridge is operating. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction is ahead.
The road curves left and then right.
The road curves right and then left.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right and then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down to drive safely through these curves.

questions.question: When can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: As long as you are not the driver.
If you sit in the back seat.
If you sit in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drink alcohol or have an open alcohol container in a vehicle on a public road. It is illegal for anyone in the vehicle, including passengers. Do not keep open alcohol in the driver or passenger area of any vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Slow down and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens, move as far right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. This applies no matter which direction the emergency vehicle is coming from.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It helps driving skills but hurts judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but hurts driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance. Alcohol makes you take more risks and lowers your caution. All of these hurt safe driving.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Use your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that it is clear.
Tell the children to stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that it is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you back up, get out and look behind your car. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially when children are near. Always check the area behind your vehicle before backing up.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When the left arm and hand point upward, the driver is signaling a right turn. If you see this signal, adjust your driving so the other vehicle can turn safely.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs mean?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers of railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and never try to drive around them.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly. When safe, pull to the side of the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in school zones?

options.text: They are reduced.
They stay the same.
They are doubled.
There are no fines.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are doubled.
questions.explanation: In Florida, fines are doubled for traffic violations in school zones. You may also face civil penalties up to $1,000 and be required to take a driving course.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the other lane is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, go to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic signals are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and go when it is your turn. Proceed with caution.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether there is a crosswalk or not.

questions.question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe distance lets you react to problems without emergency braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycles cross here.
Stop.
Fines are doubled in work zones.
Stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycles cross here.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws as if the area were not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from flaggers, signs, or police in construction zones. Not following a flagger is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when some drivers go faster or slower than others. Always drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the center of the street.
On the left side of the street.
On the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move as far to the right as possible before turning right. Do not cut across other lanes to turn.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when:

options.text: You stare at the road for a long time without paying full attention.
You take frequent rest stops.
You get too much sleep the night before.
You drive short distances on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for a long time without paying full attention.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for too long and stop checking around you. You lose focus and may not see traffic slowing or stopping ahead.

questions.question: Night driving requires extra caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
More cars are on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far or as clearly as during the day. Use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

questions.question: When can you pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk?

options.text: When the car does not drive fast enough after the pedestrian leaves.
When the pedestrian is directly in front.
When you do not see a pedestrian.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Assume any stopped vehicle is waiting for a pedestrian, even if you cannot see one.

questions.question: To avoid alcohol-related crashes, you can:

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Tell people no when they offer you a drink because you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign shows:

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
More pedestrians may be ahead.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during posted times. An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is to:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit going into the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Speed up gently before entering the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Your car's momentum may pull it away from the road. Slowing down first helps you stay in control.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes. You can do this safely as long as you do not interfere with traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about road conditions and hazards ahead. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about an upcoming intersection.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane well in advance. Do not slow down until after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and other vehicles is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between you and other vehicles. This gives you enough time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light signals.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what the other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic signals help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers must obey these signals. However, when a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of passengers.
Certain turns are allowed from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Both lanes must merge smoothly together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of passengers.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. These lanes are for buses and vehicles with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead only allows one-way traffic.
The bridge ahead fits only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about hazards ahead. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that an upcoming bridge may be too narrow to pass a truck. Be careful.

questions.question: To be ready for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Scan the entire road and all sides.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the entire road and all sides.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on finding problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but do not just stare at the center of the road. Scan the entire road and the sides too.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
Anytime.
After changing lanes.
Early so other drivers know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early so other drivers know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This lets other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians happen because drivers did not see them. These road users are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They may move faster and have dimmer lights. Always watch for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians to prevent crashes.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic on the freeway.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up and match the freeway traffic speed. This helps you blend in safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
Crossroad ahead. Be ready for traffic from other directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Be ready for traffic from other directions.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: What can help prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turning on your car radio.
Slowing down.
Stopping regularly to rest and stretch.
Moving your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take regular breaks even if you do not feel tired. Stop, rest, and stretch to stay alert.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downhill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downhill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side when you have enough distance between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: What is the main concern when you see this sign?

options.text: Your headlights may point upward because one side of your car is higher than the other.
A tire may be damaged if you drive onto the shoulder.
You may hydroplane if the shoulder is wet.
You may lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road ahead. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: After the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers go around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or train whistles. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming up.
Road construction is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane ends on a multi-lane road. Traffic in the right lane must merge to the left.
